passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: . 2025 Executive Overview 2025 was another strong year that exceeded expectations, setting new records across our business and achieving more milestones, including: • Record revenues of $26.6 billion • All-time high operating income of $4.5 billion, up 25% compared to the prior year • Achieved the highest adjusted return on invested capital (“ROIC”) in 19 years • Record booking trends with continued strong close-in demand throughout the year • Ended 2025 with record year-end customer deposits, up nearly 7% year over year In 2025, we made significant progress strengthening our balance sheet. In December 2025, we successfully completed our $19 billion refinancing plan in less than a year and reduced total debt by over $10 billion since our peak in January 2023. In addition, we surpassed our investment grade leverage metric threshold. These accomplishments enabled us to reinstate our dividend, reflecting both our confidence in the durability of our cash generation and the improvements we have made to our balance sheet. Looking forward, we are well-positioned to create even greater shareholder value over time as we continue to reinvest in our future. This will be driven by our focus on driving commercial excellence, disciplined newbuild strategy, our expansion of return-generating ship enhancement initiatives across some of our cruise lines and our exclusive destination development program. We continue to strengthen our demand generating efforts to position ourselves for success in 2026 and beyond. Our world-class cruise lines are refining their focus on target markets, sharpening marketing messages and reaching target consumers more efficiently. We are also enhancing our commercial strategies by leveraging AI to improve marketing effectiveness, deliver personalized experiences and drive efficiency gains across all our cruise lines. Together, we believe these initiatives will increase same ship revenues, drive margins and returns higher over time and help to close the price-to-value gap we offer versus land-based alternatives. In 2025, we opened our game-changing new exclusive destination, Celebration Key, Grand Bahama, which has already hosted more than one million guests since its July opening. We will continue to build on the success of Celebration Key through planned expansions at some of our other Paradise Collection properties, including RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay and Isla Tropicale (formerly Mahogany Bay) in 2026. In addition, we recently announced the development of Ensenada Bay Village - Treasures of Baja . This destination will showcase the natural beauty of Baja California, Mexico through a blend of adventure, culture and relaxation experiences while benefitting our west coast deployments. During 2025, we also continued making progress towards our sustainability goals. We reached our 2030 goal ahead of schedule, cutting greenhouse gas emissions intensity by over 20% relative to our 2019 baseline. Separately, our Less Left Over strategy helped reduce food waste by over 47%, edging closer to our 50% target set for 2030. passages.text: . You should carefully consider the following discussion of material factors, events and uncertainties that make an investment in the company’s securities risky and provide important information for the understanding of the “forward-looking” statements discussed in this Form 10-K and elsewhere. These risk factors should be read in conjunction with other information in this Form 10-K. The events and consequences discussed in these risk factors could have a material adverse effect on the company’s business, financial condition, operating results and stock price. These risk factors do not identify all risks that the company faces; operations could also be affected by factors, events, or uncertainties that are not presently known to the company or that the company currently does not consider to present material risks to its operations. Some of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below may have occurred in the past and reflect our beliefs and opinions as to the factors, events or contingencies that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. Some of the statements in this item and elsewhere in this document are “forward-looking statements.” For a discussion of those statements and of other factors to consider see the “Cautionary Note Concerning Factors That May Affect Future Results” section. The ordering and lettering of the risk factors set forth below is not intended to reflect any company indication of priority or likelihood. Operational Risk Factors a. Events and conditions around the world, including geopolitical uncertainty, war and other military actions, pandemics, inflation, higher interest rates and other general concerns impacting the ability or desire of people to travel could lead to a decline in demand for cruises as well as have significant negative impacts on our financial condition and operations. We have been, and may continue to be, impacted by the public’s concerns regarding the health, safety and security of travel, including pandemics, government travel advisories and travel restrictions, political instability and civil unrest, terrorist attacks, war and military action and other general concerns. The resulting impacts of these events, including a pause of our guest cruise operations, supply chain disruptions, impact on demand for cruises to neighboring regions and international sanctions and other measures that have been imposed, have significantly adversely affected, and may in the future significantly adversely affect, our business. These factors may also have the effect of heightening many other risks to our business, any of which could materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations. Additionally, we have been, and may continue to be, impacted by heightened regulations around customs and border control, travel bans to and from certain geographical areas, voluntary changes to our itineraries in light of geopolitical events, government policies increasing the difficulty of travel and limitations on issuing international travel visas. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and interest, leaving free cash flow that supports deleveraging. The company generated substantial operating cash flow, well above capital spending, and free cash flow represents a meaningful portion of debt. This internally generated liquidity reduces reliance on external financing for its newbuild and destination investment programs.

The issuer has reduced total debt from its peak, completed a large refinancing plan, and reinstated its dividend, signaling improved balance sheet strength. Management cites surpassing its investment grade leverage threshold. This track record of debt reduction and restored shareholder returns supports credit quality, although further progress depends on sustained cash generation.

key_risks.text: Global events such as geopolitical uncertainty, war, pandemics, inflation, and higher interest rates could reduce travel demand and materially harm operations. The risk factor explicitly notes these factors have previously caused a pause in guest cruise operations and supply chain disruptions. Such demand shocks would pressure revenue and cash flow, potentially reversing recent deleveraging progress.

Leverage remains elevated relative to sector peers, with net leverage above the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is significant, and the Altman Z double prime zone indicates distress. A moderate decline in EBITDA or increase in debt could push leverage past the next threshold, highlighting vulnerability to earnings volatility.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate but below the sector median, and free cash flow to debt is modest. Operating income covers interest expense multiple times, yet the ratio trails peers. Cash flow coverage of debt is low, indicating limited cushion for unexpected outflows. This constrains financial flexibility if operating conditions deteriorate.

The maturity profile is manageable, with no single year requiring outsized repayment. Near-term maturities are modest relative to annual operating cash flow, and the company has demonstrated access to refinancing. However, the current ratio is very low, reflecting heavy current liabilities, which could strain liquidity if cash generation weakens.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer shows improving operating performance, with revenue and operating income growing over recent years. Operating margin exceeds the sector median, and cash flow is robust. Debt reduction and refinancing have strengthened the balance sheet. However, leverage remains above peers and the indicative risk profile is significant, suggesting credit metrics are not yet investment grade on a comparative basis.

Forward-looking, the credit profile depends on sustaining demand and cash generation to further deleverage. The company plans continued investment in newbuilds and destinations, which will absorb cash. Shareholder returns have resumed, potentially competing with debt reduction. Given the significant risk profile and sector-relative weakness, the outlook is stable but sensitive to demand shocks or cost pressures.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支及利息，並產生自由現金流以支持去槓桿。公司產生龐大營運現金流，遠高於資本開支，而自由現金流佔債務一個有意義的比例。此內部產生之流動性降低其新船及目的地投資計劃對外部融資之依賴。
發行人已將總債務自高峰水平降低，完成大規模再融資計劃，並恢復派息，顯示資產負債表實力改善。管理層表示已超越其投資級槓桿門檻。此債務削減及恢復股東回報之往績支持信貸質素，惟進一步進展取決於持續現金產生能力。

key_risks.text: 地緣政治不確定性、戰爭、疫情、通脹及利率上升等全球事件可能降低旅遊需求並對營運造成重大損害。風險因素明確指出該等因素過往曾導致郵輪營運暫停及供應鏈中斷。此等需求衝擊將對收入及現金流構成壓力，可能逆轉近期去槓桿進展。
相對於同業，槓桿仍然偏高，淨槓桿高於行業中位數。指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，而Altman Z雙質數區間顯示陷入困境。EBITDA適度下降或債務增加可能將槓桿推高至下一個門檻以上，凸顯其對盈利波動之脆弱性。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率充足但低於行業中位數，而自由現金流對債務比率適度。營運收入覆蓋利息開支多倍，惟比率落後同業。現金流對債務覆蓋率偏低，顯示應對意外資金流出之緩衝有限。倘營運狀況惡化，此將限制財務靈活性。
到期結構可控，並無任何單一年份需要巨額還款。近期到期債務相對於年度營運現金流而言適度，而公司已展示再融資渠道。然而，流動比率極低，反映流動負債沉重，倘現金產生能力減弱，可能對流動性構成壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人營運表現改善，收入及營運收入於近年增長。營運利潤率超過行業中位數，而現金流穩健。債務削減及再融資已強化資產負債表。然而，槓桿仍高於同業，而指示性風險狀況為顯著，顯示信貸指標按比較基準尚未達投資級。
前瞻而言，信貸狀況取決於維持需求及現金產生能力以進一步去槓桿。公司計劃繼續投資於新船及目的地，將吸收現金。股東回報已恢復，可能與債務削減競爭。鑑於顯著風險狀況及相對於行業之弱勢，展望穩定但對需求衝擊或成本壓力敏感。
